questions.question: The ____ trailer is most likely to roll over if a driver turns too quickly.
questions.explanation: When turning, steer gently and smoothly. A quick turn while pulling trailers is dangerous. The last trailer is most likely to roll over.

questions.question: Bobtail tractors are ____ to stop than tractors with full trailers attached.
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor with no trailer attached. Bobtails are harder to stop and need more distance to come to a complete stop than tractors pulling loaded trailers.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
A valve that prevents the truck from being stolen
A valve that prevents the driver from going too fast
A valve that prevents the trailer from accidentally disconnecting

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
questions.explanation: In a combination vehicle with air brakes, the tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor's brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.

questions.question: To reduce rollover risk, you should:

options.text: Load cargo as far forward as possible.
Load cargo as far back as possible.
Load cargo as low as possible.
Stack cargo as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load cargo as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Load your cargo as close to the ground as possible. Also take curves and corners slowly to further reduce rollover risk.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be:

options.text: Slightly higher than the center of the fifth wheel.
Level with the center of the fifth wheel.
Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
Next to the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.question: A shut-off valve:

options.text: Is located on the front of a trailer.
Is located on the instrument panel.
Stops air from leaving the brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from leaving the brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve should always be closed to prevent air from leaving the brake system.

questions.question: During a trip, which shut-off valves should be open?

options.text: All shut-off valves should be open.
The rear shut-off valves should be open.
All shut-off valves should be open except the rear shut-off valves.
No shut-off valves should be open.

questions.correctAnswerText: All shut-off valves should be open except the rear shut-off valves.
questions.explanation: Before starting a trip, open all shut-off valves except the rear valves. This allows air to reach the brakes on all trailers while preventing air from escaping from the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: More than half of all truck driver accident deaths are caused by:
questions.explanation: Truck rollovers cause more than half of all truck driver accident deaths. To prevent rollovers, load cargo low and centered on your truck, and take corners slowly and carefully.

questions.question: Starting in which year were newly made trailers required to have ABS?
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: When traveling slower than 40 mph, keep at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: How should a driver test the tractor protection valve?

options.text: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve: Let the air supply charge fully. Turn off the engine. Press the brake pedal several times to release air from the system. The valve should move to its emergency position when air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: Before backing your tractor under the trailer, the trailer brakes should be:
questions.explanation: Before backing your tractor under the trailer, make sure the trailer brakes are locked. This is an important step for safely coupling and uncoupling combination vehicles.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking.
Should only be used for parking on a downgrade.
Should never be used for parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve for parking. Using it can release air pressure from the braking system and release the brakes holding the vehicle. Instead, use the parking brake or wheel chocks.

questions.question: At speeds under 40 mph, maintain a following distance of at least ____ for every 10 feet of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one extra second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: What does the trailer air supply control look like?
questions.explanation: On newer vehicles, the trailer air supply control is an eight-sided red knob. You use it to control the tractor protection valve.

questions.question: When uncoupling a trailer, the landing gear should be:
questions.explanation: Always raise the landing gear completely before driving. When uncoupling, lower the landing gear until it makes firm contact with the ground. If the trailer is loaded, turn the crank a few extra times to remove some weight from the trailer.

questions.question: Changing lanes quickly in a combination vehicle can cause:

options.text: A "crack-the-whip" effect that can cause a rollover.
Confusion about which lane the driver wants to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: A "crack-the-whip" effect that can cause a rollover.
questions.explanation: The rear of a combination vehicle swings out more than the front when turning. This "crack-the-whip" effect can cause a rollover if you change lanes too quickly.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Makes it easier to turn a large vehicle.

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your vehicle's wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: If oil and water build up in your vehicle's air tanks, the brakes:
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks daily to remove water and oil buildup. Too much oil and water in the air tanks can prevent the brakes from working properly.

questions.question: Pull out the trailer air supply control to test:
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before starting a trip. Make sure the trailer rolls freely first. Then pull out the trailer air supply control to the emergency position. Pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.
